topics.title: Individual Differences and Assessment of Psychological Attributes
topics.ncert_sections: Individual Differences in Human Functioning; Assessment of Psychological Attributes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain individual differences and how situationism accounts for behaviour through situational factors.
Identify the domains of intelligence, aptitude, interest, personality and values.
Distinguish formal from informal assessment and the methods of test, interview, case study, observation and self-report.
State how Binet, Wechsler and later theorists defined intelligence.
Describe the one-factor, two-factor, primary mental abilities, hierarchical and structure-of-intellect theories.

topics.title: Multiple Intelligences, Triarchic Theory and the PASS Model
topics.ncert_sections: Theory of Multiple Intelligences; Triarchic Theory of Intelligence; PASS Model of Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Gardner's eight independent intelligences and the persons typically high on each.
Distinguish componential, experiential and contextual intelligence in Sternberg's theory.
Explain arousal/attention, simultaneous and successive processing, and planning in the PASS model.

topics.title: Nature, Nurture and the Measurement of IQ
topics.ncert_sections: Intelligence: Interplay of Nature and Nurture; Assessment of Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret twin and adoption evidence on heredity and environment in intelligence.
Calculate IQ from mental age and chronological age, and mental age from IQ.
Interpret the normal distribution of IQ scores and the classification in Table 1.1.

topics.title: Variations of Intelligence
topics.ncert_sections: Variations of Intelligence: Intellectual Deficiency; Intellectual Giftedness

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the AAMD definition and the levels of intellectual disability.
Distinguish giftedness from talent and describe how gifted children are identified.

topics.title: Types of Intelligence Tests and Testing in India
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Intelligence Tests; Some Misuses of Intelligence Tests (Box 1.1); Intelligence Testing in India

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish individual and group, verbal, non-verbal and performance, and culture-fair and culture-biased tests.
Recognise the ill-effects of intelligence testing by untrained testers.
Identify pioneering efforts and tests in intelligence testing in India.

topics.title: Culture, Intelligence and Emotional Intelligence
topics.ncert_sections: Culture and Intelligence; Intelligence in the Indian Tradition; Emotional Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Compare technological intelligence with non-western views and Vygotsky's view of culture.
Describe integral intelligence, buddhi and the competencies valued in the Indian tradition.
Explain emotional intelligence and the characteristics of emotionally intelligent persons.

topics.title: Aptitude and Creativity
topics.ncert_sections: Special Abilities: Aptitude: Nature and Measurement; Creativity; Creativity and Intelligence

concepts.learning_objective: Explain aptitude, how it differs from interest, and how independent and multiple aptitude tests measure it.
Explain variations in creativity and the roles of heredity and environment.
Evaluate the relationship between creativity and intelligence and how creativity tests differ.
